findings.title: Appending --features=rolling-updates to the documented command can silently override the user's feature configuration
findings.body:
The `updatecompatibility` macro now appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every documented `update-compatibility` invocation. A CLI `--features` value takes precedence over `KC_FEATURES` or a `features=` entry in keycloak.conf.

A user who already enables other features would copy this command and replace their feature list with only `rolling-updates`. The `metadata` and `check` commands would then capture or compare a configuration that differs from the real deployment. The guide itself warns that omitted configuration leads to incorrect results.

The docs should tell users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list rather than hardcoding the flag.

findings.title: Docs claim the Operator fails if rolling-updates is not enabled, but this PR adds no such check
findings.body:
The new CAUTION block says that if the `rolling-updates` feature is not enabled, "the {project_name} Operator will fail." No operator code in this PR checks the feature or fails on it.

The example also enables the feature through the Keycloak CR `features` list, which configures the server and not the Operator. The test `UpgradeTest` only enables the feature when a strategy is set.

As written, the statement misleads users about what happens. Either the Operator should validate `spec.update` against the enabled features, or the text should describe the actual behavior.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is repurposed from 'recreate upgrade' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body:
`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changes from 4 to 3, and 4 now means `FEATURE_DISABLED`. Any script or automation written against the previous behavior that treats exit code 4 as "recreate required" will now get that meaning for a different condition.

The new value does align with the docs table, but the renumbering should be called out, for example in release or upgrade notes.

findings.title: Feature-disabled path tested only for 'metadata' and without checking the exit code
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only runs the `metadata` subcommand and only asserts the error message. It does not check that the exit code is `FEATURE_DISABLED` (4), which is the documented, scriptable contract. The `check` subcommand's feature-disabled branch is not tested at all.
